claims.text: Adding Si to CrFeCoNi promotes formation of a continuous, highly adherent oxide layer above 900 °C.
Adding Al to CrFeCoNi promotes formation of a continuous, highly adherent oxide layer above 900 °C.
The oxide layers formed on the Si- and Al-containing alloys grow slowly and remain coherent above 900 °C.
Mn does not provide the protective-oxide benefit attributed to Si and Al.
Cr and Si or Al selectively partition to the alloy surface during high-temperature oxidation.
Selective oxidation produces an alumina- or silica-rich surface scale.
The Si- or Al-associated protective scale has low thermal-expansion mismatch with the substrate.
The Si- or Al-associated protective scale has reduced defect density.
Cr and Si or Al diffuse to the surface at high temperature and form a dense scale with low oxygen diffusivity.
Low oxygen diffusivity causes the protective scale to grow slowly.
Chemical and lattice compatibility between the substrate and oxide reduces stress accumulation.
Reduced stress accumulation prevents oxide cracking and spallation.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNi alloys form rapidly growing, high-defect-density oxide scales.
The oxide scales on Mn-containing alloys are prone to cracking and eventual spallation.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiAl will form more stable, slower-growing, and more coherent protective oxides than CrFeCoNiMn under matched exposure conditions above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNi without a beneficial X addition does not reliably form a coherent protective scale at high temperature.
